notes.note: Cliopatria leaves Louisiana west of the Mississippi blank. France ceded it to Spain in 1762 (Treaty of Fontainebleau); Spain governed it from New Orleans until it was returned to France in 1800 and sold to the United States in 1803.

The 1815 sketch map draws all British territory north of the United States as one area (it calls it Canada). Before Confederation on 1 July 1867 these were separate British possessions: Upper and Lower Canada (one Province of Canada from 1841), the Atlantic colonies, and Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory of the Hudson's Bay Company.

Inside the United States the map fills each state from the Newberry atlas. The eleven states that seceded are filled in the Confederacy's colour from the day each passed its ordinance of secession (South Carolina first, on 20 December 1860) until the surrender of the last large Confederate army on 26 May 1865. The Union never recognised the secession, and the border states and the areas the Union army held are not drawn apart.

The borders are the ones internationally recognised on 1 July of each year (CShapes). Occupied countries keep their own colour, made faint, under diagonal lines in the occupier's colour; the year panel says which colour is which occupier. The list of occupations is written for GeoHistory. Where only a part of a country was occupied (the Soviet Union, China, France until 1942) the part is Cliopatria's outline of what Germany or Japan held in that calendar year, cut to the country; Cliopatria has one outline per year and does not say which day it stands for, so the front line is approximate. Manchukuo is OpenHistoricalMap's outline. Countries annexed outright are drawn inside their annexer, as CShapes has them.

The borders are the recognised ones on 1 July. Occupied countries keep their own colour, made faint, under diagonal lines in the occupier's colour (Belgium and Luxembourg from 1914, Serbia from late 1915, Montenegro from 1916, most of Romania from late 1916). Occupied northern France and the occupied west of Russia are Cliopatria's outline of what Germany held in that calendar year (none for 1914), cut to the country: one outline per year, so the front is approximate.

CShapes draws Manchuria as part of China. From 1 March 1932 to August 1945 it was Manchukuo, a state set up and controlled by Japan that most countries did not recognise: it is shown by lines in Japan's colour over China's, from OpenHistoricalMap's outline.

Cliopatria draws the Mongol Empire as one state until 1294. After the succession war of 1260 to 1264 it was in practice four: the Yuan dynasty of Kublai Khan in the east, the Golden Horde, the Chagatai Khanate and the Ilkhanate.

The source gives the Gorkha Kingdom the outline of later Nepal. Until Prithvi Narayan Shah's conquests (the Kathmandu Valley fell in 1768) Gorkha was one small hill state among dozens, and the valley was ruled by the Malla kings of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur.

Cliopatria has no Maratha state for these years and draws the whole Deccan as Mughal. After the execution of Sambhaji in 1689 the Marathas under Rajaram and Tarabai fought on from their forts and were never fully conquered; they expanded again after Aurangzeb's death in 1707.

Much of western and central India is blank on the source map in these years. It was not empty: the Rajput states (Mewar among them) and, from 1401 and 1407, the sultanates of Malwa and Gujarat ruled there.

The sources draw only the Hejaz here. By Muhammad's death in June 632 most of the Arabian Peninsula acknowledged the Muslim state centred on Medina; the Rashidun Caliphate appears on the map from 633.

The sketch map still gives all of central and southern Africa to Khoisan hunter-gatherers and herders. By about AD 300 to 500 Bantu-speaking farmers had settled most of central, eastern and south-eastern Africa, and Khoisan peoples remained mainly in the south-west.

This sketch-map area is far too large for these years. Bantu languages began to spread from the border region of today's Nigeria and Cameroon only in the last two or three millennia BC; the band across Africa shown here is not a Bantu homeland.

The source outline for the Danish settlement in Bengal is misplaced: it covers Calcutta, which was the capital of British Bengal. The Danish settlement was Serampore (Frederiksnagore), about 20 km to the north, held from 1755 to 1845.

Cliopatria takes Congress Poland (Warsaw) out of the Russian Empire for 1830 to 1833 and calls it "Poles". Poland was under the Russian tsar from 1815; Polish insurgents controlled it only during the November Uprising, from 29 November 1830 to October 1831. It is shown as a Russian possession in 1830, 1832 and 1833 and as the insurgent kingdom in 1831.

Cliopatria leaves Athens, Attica, the Aegean islands and several colonies blank for these years; they are filled from the sketch map of 500 BC as "Greek cities (city-states and colonies)". Athens was an independent city-state and led the Delian League from 478 BC to 404 BC.

During the Iberian Union (1580 to 1640) the kings of Spain were also kings of Portugal. Cliopatria draws Portugal's possessions, such as Brazil, as part of the Spanish Empire in these years; they stayed a separate Portuguese crown with their own administration.

Cliopatria draws Spain's American possessions as one territory. They were governed as viceroyalties: New Spain (Mexico City) from 1535 and Peru (Lima) from 1542, later also New Granada (1717) and the Río de la Plata (1776).
Cliopatria draws British possessions as one territory. From 1 July 1867 Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick formed the self-governing Dominion of Canada inside the British Empire.

The sketch map calls this coast "Islamic city-states": these are the Swahili city-states of East Africa (Mogadishu, Mombasa, Zanzibar, Kilwa). The strongest of them in the 13th to 15th centuries was the Kilwa Sultanate, which the Portuguese took in 1505.

Cliopatria's Maratha state of these years does not reach Raigad, Shivaji's capital, which it draws inside the Mughal Empire. Shivaji was crowned at Raigad in 1674 and held the western Deccan hill country until his death in 1680.
Portuguese Goa (taken from Bijapur in 1510) is too small for Cliopatria's outline and is drawn inside the Bijapur Sultanate.
Cliopatria keeps Kandahar and Kabul inside Afsharid Iran for some years after 1747, the year Ahmad Shah Durrani founded the Durrani Empire at Kandahar.
From 270 to 273 Queen Zenobia's Palmyrene Empire held Syria, Egypt and much of Asia Minor; Cliopatria draws these provinces as Roman throughout.
The Kingdom of Dahomey (capital Abomey) paid tribute to Oyo from 1730 to 1823 and is drawn inside it.
Cliopatria draws the whole east coast of Iberia as Greek city-states. The Greek colonies (Emporion, Rhode) were few; most of this coast was held by Iberian peoples.

The blank in central India is the Malwa Sultanate (1401 to 1531, capital Mandu) with Khandesh and the Gond kingdoms: no source used here has an outline for them. The Gajapati kingdom's outline is the sketch map's small Orissa and does not reach its capital Cuttack.

Between the Rhine, the Danube and the Vistula the sources have outlines only for a few peoples; the rest of Germania (Suebi, Semnones, Lombards, Goths and others) is left blank rather than drawn by hand.

Cliopatria keeps Egypt inside the Assyrian Empire until 616 BC (and names the whole empire "Assyrian Egypt" in these years, corrected here). Psamtik I of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty had made Egypt independent by about 655 BC.

Cliopatria files the lands Alexander took from Persia between 331 and 324 BC under "Ptolemaic Kingdom". Ptolemy became satrap of Egypt only in 323 BC and king in 305 BC; these rows are shown as Alexander's conquests, part of the Macedonian Empire.

Khwarezm itself (the lower Amu Darya) and Transoxiana are blank in these years. The Mongols conquered them in 1219 to 1221, but Cliopatria adds them to the Mongol Empire only from 1227; it keeps a Khwarezmid Empire in Iran and Afghanistan, whose outline is shown from 1222 (see the Khwarezmid Empire).

Western Iran after the Mongol general Chormaqan destroyed the state of Jalal al-Din, the last Khwarezmshah, in 1230 to 1231. The outline is Cliopatria's Khwarezmid Empire of 1227 to 1235; much of it (Fars, Kerman) was held by local rulers who paid tribute to the Mongols.

The map shows the borders in law. German armies occupied northern and eastern France from August 1870; after the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871), which gave Alsace and part of Lorraine to the German Empire, the occupied departments were evacuated step by step as France paid its indemnity, the last in September 1873. Cliopatria draws the occupied area as German in 1870 to 1872 (Paris included); that is corrected here, and 1870 keeps the borders of before the war, which began on 19 July.

Cliopatria draws the Tang empire whole until its end. After the Huang Chao rebellion (874 to 884) the court controlled little outside the capital region, and the provinces were ruled by military governors, whose regimes became the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms after 907.

names: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms (former Tang lands)
notes.note: The Tang dynasty ended in 907, when Zhu Wen deposed the last emperor and founded the Later Liang at Kaifeng. Cliopatria keeps the whole Tang outline until 910 and draws the separate states (Later Liang, Jin, Former Shu, Wu, Wuyue, Chu, Min and others) only from 911, so these four years show the former Tang lands as one area.

The last kings of Mitanni (Hanigalbat) were vassals of Assyria, and Shalmaneser I made the country an Assyrian province about 1260 BC. Cliopatria draws a Mitanni state until 1241 BC; from 1259 BC it is shown as an Assyrian possession. Dates this early are uncertain by a decade or more.

Cliopatria calls this area Great Moravia from 814. Great Moravia is dated from about 833, when Mojmir I joined the principality of Nitra to Moravia; the Moravians are first named in Frankish annals in 822.

The Hoysala king Veera Ballala III was killed at Madurai in 1343 and his son Ballala IV is last heard of in 1346; their lands passed to the Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara I in 1336. Cliopatria draws a Hoysala kingdom until 1351; from 1347 its outline is shown as part of Vijayanagara.
The outline is the sketch map's Travancore of 1815: Cliopatria has no shape for the kingdom, founded by Marthanda Varma in 1729.

The outline is Cliopatria's Khwarezmid Empire of 1227 to 1235, which reaches the Indus, and is larger than what the Khwarezmian princes held. After the Mongol campaign of 1219 to 1221 Ghiyath al-Din held Persian Iraq and Kerman, and Jalal al-Din, back from India in 1224, ruled western Iran and from 1225 Azerbaijan, until the Mongol general Chormaqan destroyed his state in 1230 to 1231. Khorasan and Afghanistan, sacked by the Mongols in 1220 to 1221, were held by no lasting power in these years.

Most of the tribes of inner and eastern Arabia sent delegations to Muhammad in 630 and 631 (the Year of Delegations) and acknowledged the Muslim state at Medina, which the sources draw only in the Hejaz. Many broke away at his death in June 632; Abu Bakr brought them back in the Ridda Wars of 632 and 633.
Cliopatria still draws Yemen as Sasanian. Badhan, the Persian governor of Yemen, accepted Islam in 628, and Yemen was no longer ruled from Ctesiphon.
